To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated for the first time the conjugative mobilization of an Enterococcus plasmid containing the vancomycin resistance transposons Tn1546 by a putative E. faecum sex pheromones response plasmid (pHKK703).
we have identified a novel mechanism for the conjugative mobilization of the Tn1546-containing plasmid pHKK702, which encodes VanA resistance.
a vancomycin resistant plasmid from Enterococcus faeium is conjugatively mobilizable by a plasmid that carries the genes for the E. faeium sex pheromo response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mobilization of vancomycin-resistant plasmids in enterococci.

the mobilization of a Tn1547-like transposon by a putative sex pheromones response plasmid in Enterococcus faeium, and the possible implications of this mobilization on the spread of vancomycin-resistant enterococci.
the mechanisms by which vancomycin resistance genes are transferred between enterococci.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the E. fae cium strain R7 contains a vancomycin-resistant plasmid, pHKK702, which can be mobilized by the sex pher omone response plasm id pHKK703, and this mobilization may be mediated by donor-mediated recombination.
pHKK702 is mobilized by pHKK703, and that the mechanism of mobilization is conjugation.
pHKK702 and the sex pheromon response plasmid pHKK703 are involved in the conjugative transfer of vancomycin and erythromycin resistances in E. faecum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that a plasmid carrying the vancomycin resistance transposone Tn1546 can be mobilized by a sex pheromones response plasmid.

the Vmr plasmid pHKK702 is mobilized by a putative E. faecimum sex pheromome response plasmid pHK703, and this mobilization is enhanced in a donor strain that is proficient for donor-mediated recombination.
a putative E. faecum sex pheromome response plasmid (pHKK703) conjugatively mobilizes a Tn1547-like element (pHKK702) that carries the Vmr determinant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mobilization of the vancomycin resistance element by a putative sex pheromome response plasmid may represent a mechanism for the dissemination of vancomcyin resistance among E. faecum isolates.
the mobilization of Tn1546-containing plasmids by E. faecum sex pheromones could be a significant mechanism of horizontal gene transfer of vancomycin-resistance genes in hospitals.
the mobilization of the vancomycin resistance transposons is not a simple matter of plasmid transfer.
